newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PT future could herald EDP, BCP contracts.
newsitem.headline: PT future could herald EDP, BCP contracts.

text.p: The launch of the first futures contract on an individual Portuguese share, Portugal Telecom, on Friday brings liquidity and depth to the market and may precede similar contracts in blue chips such as EDP and BCP.
Oporto Derivatives Exchange (BDP) presently trades futures on the PSI20 index of leading Portuguese stocks, 10-year bonds and three-month Lisbor.
"The PT futures contract is another risk management instrument," said Antonio Aranha of Cisf Dealer, one of the market makers.
Market makers said they believed that futures contracts would eventually be launched in other leading stocks, including Banco Comercial Portugues and privatised utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal.
"The next stocks that will have futures contracts are those with the biggest capitalisation and liquidity," said Ana Matos of Banco Portugues de Investimento. "BCP and EDP are two examples."
Francisco Faria of Lisbon broker Eser said: "This (PT futures contract) will be the first step, and perhaps in 1998 we will be ready to launch an options market."
An options market would be an alternative to "short selling", which has been used seldom even though it has been regulated, analysts said.
"The new futures contract on PT is attracting attention because it will boost liquidity," said Faria.
Aranha said that if the PT futures contract proved to be a success, similar contracts in other blue chips would follow shortly afterwards.
Carlos Goncalves of Central Banco de Investimentos said he believed small investors would trade actively in PT futures as they had already done in PSI20 futures.
"This is a bold step of the BDP," he said. "But we'll have to wait until after the summer to see a surge in liquidity."
Matos said the first few days of trade in the PT future would probably be calm. The contract did not trade on its first session due to communications problems on the BDP.
Analysts noted that one of the reasons for the recent promotion of the Lisbon bourse to the status of a developed market by Morgan Stanley was the recent launch of futures trade.
The market makers on the PT futures will be Banco Portugues de Investimento, Central Banco de Investimento and Cisf Dealer.
The unit of trade in the futures contract is 100 PT shares, and the minimum variation in the share will be one tick, that is one escudo.
